title: Annapurna Trekking

source.notes: Rewritten into Brian's chapter format from the YouLi copy. No facts added; open questions are in reviewNotes.

reviewNotes: Day numbering: YouLi says 15 days but lists Days 1–13, then Day 16 (free day) and Day 17 (departure). I have shown those as Days 14 and 15. Confirm.
Jomsom, Day 11: YouLi gives a sleeping altitude of 3,760 m / 12,332 ft, the same as Muktinath the night before. Is that right?
What is in the $3,100? YouLi has no included or not-included list (trek lodging, meals, permits, the two domestic flights?), and no price basis (double occupancy?).
Lodging: YouLi names no hotels in Kathmandu or Pokhara and does not say what kind of lodging is used on the trek. I have listed overnights by place only.

seo.title: Annapurna Circuit Trek — 15 Days in Nepal | Adventure Access
seo.description: Fifteen days from Kathmandu around the Annapurna Circuit: Manang, Thorong La at 17,769 feet, Jomsom and Pokhara. From $3,100.

hero.title: Annapurna
hero.subtitle: The classic circuit: deep gorges, Tibetan villages and a pass at 17,769 feet
hero.imageAlt: A trekker on a grassy trail below snow peaks

intro.label: The Journey
intro.heading: One of Nepal's Great Treks
paragraphs: The Annapurna Circuit is one of the greatest treks in Nepal, and one of the most varied. Deep gorges, high mountain passes, Buddhist temples, ethnic Tibetan peoples, farming villages and all the major mountains of the Annapurna Massif.

The trip starts and ends in Kathmandu, where our guides meet you at the airport and handle the details. From there it is a jeep ride to Besisahar and Chame, a week on foot up the Marshyangdi valley and over Thorong La, and two short mountain flights back by way of Pokhara.

dayTypes.label: How the Days Work
dayTypes.heading: Drive In, Walk Over, Fly Out
dayTypes.lede: The trek climbs steadily from Chame to the pass, with a rest day in Manang to help your body adjust before the hardest day of the trip.

cards.title: City days
cards.body: Days 1–2 and 13–15 in Kathmandu: a cultural tour in Boudha, a trek orientation, a celebration dinner in Thamel and a free day.

cards.title: Trekking days
cards.body: Days 5–11: four to nine hours on foot each day, with a rest day in Manang on Day 7 and the crossing of Thorong La on Day 10.

cards.title: Travel days
cards.body: Days 3–4 are 6–7 hour jeep drives to Besisahar and Chame. Days 12–13 are short flights from Jomsom to Pokhara and on to Kathmandu.

chapters.label: The Journey in Chapters
chapters.heading: Around the Annapurna Massif
chapters.lede: Altitudes are where you sleep each night unless noted.

groups.title: Kathmandu — Arrival and Orientation

image.alt: The eyes of Boudhanath stupa under prayer flags

prose: Your guide meets you at the airport, so there is no need to find your hotel in the back alleys of Boudha or Thamel on your own. There is still plenty of time to explore the city, eat well and get to know your guide before the mountains.

days.label: Day 1
days.text: Arrive in Kathmandu, meet your guide and transfer to your hotel.

days.label: Day 2
days.text: A cultural tour in Boudha, the trip orientation, and dinner with your guide and group.

groups.title: Besisahar and Chame — Up the Marshyangdi

image.alt: Jeeps and vans on a road below green hills

prose: Two days by jeep take you out of the city. Besisahar is the headquarters of Lamjung District, and Chame, reached along the Marshyangdi River, is the headquarters of Manang District and the start of the trek.

days.label: Day 3
days.text: A 6–7 hour drive by reserved jeep to Besisahar. Sleeping altitude 2,490 ft.

days.label: Day 4
days.text: A 6–7 hour drive by jeep to Chame. Sleeping altitude 8,692 ft.

groups.title: Pisang and Manang — Into the Gorge

image.alt: Trekkers crossing a long suspension bridge through the forest

prose: The trail crosses and recrosses the gorge carved by the Marshyangdi River on suspension bridges before it reaches Manang, the largest village on the route. A full day there lets your body adjust before the climb to the pass.

days.label: Day 5
days.text: Trek to Pisang, about 5–6 hours. Sleeping altitude 10,660 ft.

days.label: Day 6
days.text: Trek to Manang, about 5–6 hours. Sleeping altitude 11,545 ft.

days.label: Day 7
days.text: A rest day. Take it easy, walk around Manang and go to bed early to prepare for the ascent to Thorong La.

groups.title: Thorong La — The True Test
groups.badge: ✦ The high point of the circuit

image.alt: Prayer flags covering the sign at the top of Thorong La pass

prose: Thorong High Camp and the pass itself, at 5,416 m or 17,769 ft, are the true physical test of this itinerary. The crossing is the longest day of the trek, ending in Muktinath.

days.label: Day 8
days.text: Trek to Ladar, about 4–5 hours. Sleeping altitude 13,776 ft.

days.label: Day 9
days.text: Trek to Thorong High Camp, about 4–5 hours. Sleeping altitude about 16,137 ft.

days.label: Day 10
days.text: Over Thorong La at 17,769 ft and down to Muktinath, an 8–9 hour day. Sleeping altitude 12,332 ft.

groups.overnight: Ladar, Thorong High Camp, then Muktinath

groups.title: Jomsom and Pokhara — Down to the Lake

image.alt: Wooden boats on Phewa Lake in Pokhara

prose: From the pass the trail descends, with plenty of up and down, to Jomsom. A short flight then takes you to Pokhara on the shore of Phewa Lake, a laid-back city very different from Kathmandu.

days.label: Day 12
days.text: A flight of about 19 minutes to Pokhara, and an evening to enjoy the town.

groups.title: Kathmandu — Celebration and Home

image.alt: Snow peaks above a glacier under a blue sky

prose: Back in the capital for a dinner with your guides and a day to yourself before the flight home.

days.label: Day 13
days.text: A flight of about 30 minutes to Kathmandu, then a celebration dinner with your guides in Thamel.

days.label: Day 14
days.text: A free day. Rest, revisit your favorite places from the start of the trip, and repack for the journey home.

days.label: Day 15
days.text: Your guide picks you up at the hotel and takes you to the airport for your flight.

pullQuote: An incredibly varied and extraordinarily beautiful journey.

highlights.title: Thorong La
highlights.body: The pass at 17,769 feet, reached from a high camp at about 16,137 feet. The hardest and longest day of the trip.
highlights.imageAlt: A trekker sitting on a ridge between dark mountains

highlights.title: A Day to Adjust
highlights.body: A rest day in the largest village on the route, with time to walk and explore before the climb to the pass.
highlights.imageAlt: Trekkers at a prayer-flag cairn pointing toward snow peaks

highlights.title: Mountain Flights
highlights.body: Two short flights, Jomsom to Pokhara and Pokhara to Kathmandu. Small planes like these are a classic part of travel in Nepal.
highlights.imageAlt: Passengers boarding a small mountain plane on the runway

goodToKnow.label: Good to Know
goodToKnow.heading: Before You Go
goodToKnow.lede: A few things that shape how this trip runs.

cards.title: Kathmandu
cards.body: Your guide meets you at the airport and takes care of the details. Your time in the city includes good food, getting to know your guide and an orientation for the trek.

cards.title: Acclimatization
cards.body: A rest day in Manang on Day 7 helps your body adjust to the high altitudes on the trek. Expect an easy walk and an early night.

cards.title: Thorong La
cards.body: Thorong High Camp and the pass at 17,769 feet are the true physical test of this trip. The crossing day is 8–9 hours on foot.

cards.title: Mountain flights
cards.body: Two short flights close the trek: Jomsom to Pokhara and Pokhara to Kathmandu.

cards.title: Pokhara
cards.body: Nepal's second most populous city sits on the shore of Phewa Lake at only 2,696 feet. Dhaulagiri, Annapurna I and Manaslu are all within 35 miles of the valley.
